### David’s Return to Jerusalem
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/davids-return-to-jerusalem
Passage: 2 Samuel 19:5
Points:
- Joab killed Absalom and fiercely rebuked David to protect the king and preserve the realm.
- David's excessive mourning turned a vital victory into public humiliation for his loyal troops.
- Joab warned the king that failing to acknowledge those who saved him would forfeit their allegiance.
- Though sharp, Joab's rebuke functioned as the faithful wound of a friend that brought David to his senses.
- Leaders must be mindful to express genuine appreciation to those who support and serve alongside them.

### Day 69: 2 Samuel 19:1–8
Author: Beth Moore
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/plus/books/portraits-of-devotion/portraits-of-devotion-day-69-2-samuel-19-18.html
Passage: 2 Samuel 19:1-8
Points:
- David's grief over Absalom's death consumed him and left God's chosen nation in turmoil.
- Joab confronted the king harshly as a military commander rather than consoling him gently as a friend.
- Joab bluntly warned David that ignoring the men who fought for him would cause them to abandon him.
- Even though Joab lacked compassion, David recognized that the commander's practical counsel was right.
- By getting up and sitting at the city gate, David stepped out of isolation and became accessible once again.
